new_packages.label: תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, הַצַּדִּיק, וְתוֹרַת חֶסֶד
new_packages.label_en: Oral Torah, the Tzaddik, and the Torah of Lovingkindness
new_packages.reason: Package 2 is entirely absent from the current dataset for Torah #207 (no bechina edges connect these nodes for reference 207). It is derived from two consecutive identity-declarations in lines 8–9 of the source text. The three bechina relationships are: (1) תורה שבעל פה ↔ צדיק הדור — declared 'one thing literally' (דָּבָר אֶחָד מַמָּשׁ), the strongest possible identity formula; (2) תלמיד חכם ↔ תורה שבעל פה — 'הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ הַתּוֹרָה' (he IS himself the Torah), an equally explicit identity statement; (3) תורה שבעל פה ↔ תורת חסד — 'הַיְנוּ לְלַמֵּד לַאֲחֵרִים' (that is to say: to teach others), the bechina-formula 'הַיְנוּ' introducing the equivalence between the Torah that the tzaddik embodies and the Torah of lovingkindness he transmits. These three nodes — תורה שבעל פה, צדיק הדור (with תלמיד חכם as its generalized form), and תורת חסד — form a single bechina package because they are all expressions of the same spiritual reality: the living, embodied, outward-flowing divine teaching-presence. Neither produces the others; they are three aspects of the same thing. Polarity is unambiguously good: this is the domain of holiness, Torah, righteous leadership, and kindness.

proposed_bechina_edges.proof: כְּשֶׁמְּדַבְּרִים עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, אוֹ כְּשֶׁמְּדַבְּרִים עַל הַצַּדִּיק הַדּוֹר בְּעַצְמוֹ, הוּא דָּבָר אֶחָד מַמָּשׁ, כִּי עִקַּר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא תָּלוּי בְּצַדִּיק הַדּוֹר
הַתַּלְמִיד חָכָם הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ הַתּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מכות כב:): כַּמָּה טִפְּשָׁאֵי וְכוּ דְּקָיְמִי מִקַּמֵּי אוֹרַיְתָא וְכוּ'

אֲזַי הוּא חוֹזֵר וְעוֹשֶׂה מֵהַדִּבּוּרִים תּוֹרָה, וַאֲזַי עוֹשֶׂה תּוֹרַת חֶסֶד, הַיְנוּ לְלַמֵּד לַאֲחֵרִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוכה מט:) עַל פָּסוּק: וְתוֹרַת חֶסֶד עַל לְשׁוֹנָהּ – זֶה הַלּוֹמֵד עַל מְנָת לְלַמְּדָהּ

new_packages.structural_role: Package 2 is the resolution domain of Torah #207. The Torah's entire causal arc moves from Package 1 (speech = gevurot, requiring sweetening) through the tzaddik's action and toward Package 2 (Torah = tzaddik = torat chesed, the domain into which sweetened gevurot flow). The relationship between the two packages is: [Package 1: speech/gevurot (neutral)] →eitza→ [sweetening action by tzaddik] →eitza→ [Package 2: Torah/tzaddik/torat chesed (good)]. Package 1 represents the raw material (all speech, including harsh gevurot); Package 2 represents the actualized, holy form of that same speech-energy once it has been sweetened and transmitted as Torah. The historical-practical section (lines 2–7, centered on the Baal Shem Tov's passing) constitutes the eitza chain that explains what happens when the bridge between the packages fails: when the tzaddik cannot accomplish the sweetening, Package 2's domain is attacked (through speech against Torah she-be'al peh = speech against the tzaddik) and the tzaddik suffers or passes.
new_packages.evil_mirror_check: Torah #207 does not contain an evil bechina package that mirrors Package 2. The negative domain — false leaders (Sha'tz), seduced scholars, speech against Torah she-be'al peh — is described narratively as an eitza chain of causation and historical event. The Rebbe does not declare 'the false leader IS an aspect of X' or 'heretical speech IS a bechina of Y.' The absence of an evil mirror package is consistent with the Torah's practical orientation: its purpose is to explain the tzaddik's burden and provide tools for sweetening, not to map the ontology of the evil side. The evil is present as the force that attacks Package 2's domain — not as a structured bechina cluster of its own.

observations: Torah #207 contains exactly one new package proposal (Package 2: Torah she-be'al peh / tzaddik / talmid chakham / torat chesed). Package 1 (דיבורים = גבורות) is already represented in the dataset by edge id 602. The new package is derived from three explicit identity declarations in lines 8–9, each using the strongest available bechina language: 'דָּבָר אֶחָד מַמָּשׁ' (one literal thing), 'הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ הַתּוֹרָה' (he IS himself the Torah), and 'הַיְנוּ' introducing the equivalence between Torah and torat chesed. All three proposed bechina edges are currently absent from torahData.js for reference 207. Adding them would fully represent Torah #207's two-package structure in the graph, capturing both the Torah's foundational axiom (Package 1) and its theological depth and practical resolution (Package 2). The Torah is modest in scale (9 lines, 2 packages, 6 total nodes across both packages) but carries significant theological weight through the historical illustration of the Baal Shem Tov's passing — making it one of the most personally grounded teachings in Likutay Moharan Vol. 1.
